pass_summary: D1–D6 are implemented as planned: the scope comes from the command only, `[]` counts as absent, a name-filtered run skips confirm_green, neither tracker downgrades RED, the missing-project set is a 400 with a log line and a once-per-day notice, and plugin.json is baked before embed and verified afterwards. The splits keep module state in one place. The main defect is in the command parser: a bare test filename (a bun/vitest substring filter such as `bun test x.test.ts` run from the repo root) is resolved against cwd to a path that does not exist. That produces a non-empty scope that matches nothing, so the transition never happens. The CI permissions could also be tighter.

issues.title: Bare test-file filters resolve to non-existent paths and scope the run to nothing
issues.description: src/utils/test-run-scope.ts:215-216 (scopeFromArgs) runs `resolve(cwd, a)` on each positional and accepts it as a test file when `isTestFile(abs)` is true. isTestFile only checks the name, not whether the file exists. bun (and vitest/jest) treat positionals as path SUBSTRING filters unless they start with ./ or /. So `bun test tdd-routes.test.ts` run from the repo root actually runs src/sidecar/tdd-routes.test.ts, but the parser returns files=[<root>/tdd-routes.test.ts]. That scope is non-empty, so isScoped() is true and the route never falls back to project-wide. rowMatchesTestScope matches nothing: the forward companion, the stored test_file_path and implCandidates(<root>/tdd-routes.test.ts)=<root>/tdd-routes.ts all miss. Result: a failing run never promotes TEST_WRITTEN→RED_CONFIRMED and a passing run never clears RED, so the agent stays blocked by the TDD guard. This is a regression from the old project-wide behaviour, and it breaks D2's promise that the scope is never empty. The same happens for any relative filter that is not the literal path from cwd (e.g. `bun test sidecar/tdd-routes.test.ts` from the root). The Task 1 fixture list has no case for this.
issues.suggested_fix: In scopeFromArgs (test-run-scope.ts:215-218), accept a positional as a file only if `statSync(abs).isFile()` succeeds. Otherwise treat it as a filter: either set `unknown = true` (→ project-wide, the conservative D2 fallback), or keep the raw token as a suffix filter and extend rowMatchesTestScope to match `t.endsWith(sep + token)` against the row's expected/stored test paths. Add fixtures to src/utils/test-run-scope.test.ts for `bun test x.test.ts` from the repo root where the file lives in src/…, and for `bun test sidecar/x.test.ts`, each asserting project-wide or a correct match. Also add a route-level test showing that a failing run still confirms RED.

issues.title: Workflow-level `contents: write` now also applies to pull_request test runs
issues.description: .github/workflows/release.yml:9-10 grants `permissions: contents: write` to the whole workflow, and this change adds a `pull_request` trigger. For PRs from forks, GitHub downgrades GITHUB_TOKEN to read-only and withholds secrets, so there is no direct exfiltration path. For PRs from branches in the same repo, however, the `test` job now runs unmerged PR code (`bun install` lifecycle scripts, tests, eslint plugins) with a write-scoped token that actions/checkout persists into .git/config by default. Only the release job needs write access. The release gate itself is correct: `if: github.event_name == 'push'` (release.yml, release job) combined with `push: branches: [main]` means release never runs on a PR.
issues.suggested_fix: Set the top level to `permissions: { contents: read }`. Add `permissions: { contents: write, issues: write, pull-requests: write }` (whatever semantic-release needs) only on the `release` job. Optionally add `persist-credentials: false` to the test job's checkout, and a `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} }` block.

issues.title: Scoped transition selects outside the transaction and writes without the project/spec predicate
issues.description: src/sidecar/tdd-routes.ts scopedTransition (≈:95-138) runs the SELECT before `db.transaction(...)`, and the UPDATE/DELETE filter only on `file_path = ? AND state = ?`. This is safe today: tdd_cycles.file_path is UNIQUE (migrations-legacy.ts:200) and the state guard makes each write idempotent, so the project scope is never widened. It is fragile, though, if the uniqueness ever becomes (project_path, file_path).
issues.suggested_fix: Move the SELECT inside the transaction closure and add `AND project_path = ?${specClause}` (with scopeParams) to both write statements. That makes the project scope explicit in the write, not only in the selection.

issues.title: `cd` handling edge cases in the command parser
issues.description: src/utils/test-run-scope.ts:242-245 applies `cd` to every later segment. Two consequences: (1) a subshell `(cd sub && bun test a.test.ts); bun test b.test.ts` resolves b.test.ts under `sub`; (2) `cd -`, `cd ~/x` and `cd $DIR` resolve literally (`<cwd>/-`, `<cwd>/~/x`). Either way the paths are wrong, which leads to the empty-match failure described in the first issue.
issues.suggested_fix: Treat a `cd` target that starts with `-`, `~` or `$`, or that is not an existing directory, as unknown (return project-wide). Restore cwd at a closing `)` op by tracking a stack in the segment loop.

issues.title: Plugin resolves relative test paths against the workspace root, not the shell's actual cwd
issues.description: targets/opencode/plugins/sentinal.ts:878-881 uses `projectWorkspace` when `args.workdir` is absent. When the OpenCode session directory is a subdirectory of the checkout, the bash tool runs there, so relative args resolve to the wrong absolute paths (again an empty match).
issues.suggested_fix: Use the plugin's session/instance directory (the `directory` passed to the plugin) as the base for `workdir`, falling back to projectWorkspace.

issues.title: A blank/null projectPath on `set` is rejected without the log line or notice
issues.description: src/sidecar/tdd-routes.ts handleSetTddState (≈:279-289) logs and notifies only when `body.projectPath === undefined`. A `null` or `""` project gets a silent 400. This matches D4's wording ("absent") but would hide a buggy current client.
issues.suggested_fix: Always write the `MISSING_TDD_SET_PROJECT_LOG` line on a set-400, and call notifyMissingTddProjectOnce only when the field is absent. Tag the log line with `(blank)` vs `(absent)`.
